articles.title: India Rebased Its GDP, but Rs 34.5 Lakh Crore of Women's Work Counts for Nothing

articles.title: India's 10-Year Yield Falls to 7.07% as Democrats' Sweep Cuts Oil and US Yields
articles.excerpt: Benchmark Indian bond yields dropped 12 basis points after the US midterm result, as falling crude, a stronger rupee and lower Treasury yields combined — and fund managers say the December RBI review is now the key test.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. India's 10-year government bond yield fell to 7.07 percent as a Democrats' sweep in the US midterms cut oil prices and US yields.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian and NRI bond investors, gilt and long-duration fund values have risen with the rally; the practical question is the December RBI review, not chasing duration now.

articles.title: Sensex Surges 1,419 Points as Crude Crashes After US Midterm Sweep
articles.excerpt: The Sensex jumped 1,418.56 points to 78,719.96 and the Nifty rose past 24,300 on November 5, as Brent crude fell close to 10 per cent to around $94 after Democrats swept the US midterms.

articles.title: Advanced Micro Devices Earnings Beat as Data Center Revenue Nearly Doubles

articles.image_caption: Advanced Micro Devices headquarters in Santa Clara, California. AMD reported record third-quarter revenue as data center sales nearly doubled.
articles.nri_angle: AMD is a widely held US semiconductor stock, and its AI data-center results move the technology shares many diaspora investors track.

articles.title: McDonald's Earnings Beat Estimates Despite Revenue Miss
articles.excerpt: Adjusted EPS rose 11% to $3.57 as franchised margins grew, but revenue of $7.16 billion missed estimates and U.S. comparable sales slipped 0.2%; the dividend rises 4% to $1.93.
articles.image_caption: A McDonald's restaurant. The chain beat third-quarter earnings estimates despite a revenue miss.
articles.nri_angle: McDonald's is one of the most widely held US consumer stocks and a common first employer in diaspora communities; its U.S. sales trend is a read on lower-income consumer spending.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uber Technologies Q3 Earnings Miss on Investment Loss as Bookings Jump 20%

articles.image_caption: Uber headquarters in San Francisco. Uber's third-quarter bookings jumped 20 percent, though an investment loss weighed on earnings.
articles.nri_angle: Uber is a daily-use service for diaspora riders and a major gig platform for immigrant drivers and couriers; its bookings and autonomy plans affect both.

articles.title: Booking Holdings Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Misses on FTC Charge

articles.image_caption: Booking Holdings, parent of Booking.com, beat third-quarter earnings estimates as revenue missed on an FTC charge.

articles.excerpt: The Cabinet cleared a 30% capital subsidy for two lithium and two nickel plants over FY 2026-27 to 2030-31, with winners chosen on the lowest support sought and paid in three milestone-linked tranches.
articles.image_caption: An open-pit mining operation and mineral specimens in a WION graphic on India's critical minerals plans. The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 2,814-crore incentive scheme for domestic lithium and nickel processing plants.

articles.title: India's Middle Class Borrows Faster Than Incomes as Debt Hits Record
articles.excerpt: Household borrowing surged 36% in a year to a record 46% of GDP, while debt service climbed to about 13% of income and real pay for salaried workers rose less than 4% over three years.
articles.image_caption: Shoppers crowd a market street in Mumbai. Household borrowing in India has risen to a record 46 percent of GDP even as real earnings for salaried workers have barely grown.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family finances, property and consumer loans in India, a record debt load and expected further RBI rate hikes point to higher repayment costs for households back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Democratic Congress Puts AI Spending and Chip Export Controls Under New Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: With Democrats back in control of Congress, analysts expect tighter scrutiny of AI chip exports to China, new cost rules for large data centres, and investigations into the tariff and investment deals of the Trump administration.
articles.image_caption: A Samsung flag and the SK hynix logo at a company building. South Korea’s chipmakers face tighter scrutiny of AI chip exports and US investment pledges after the Democratic midterm victory.
articles.nri_angle: Indian investors holding US AI and chip stocks, and professionals in the Asian semiconductor supply chain, face a new oversight regime in Washington.

articles.title: Cabinet Clears Rs 14,500 Crore Storage Fund Backing 92 GWh of New Grid Capacity

articles.nri_angle: The scheme is a direct read on where India grid-scale storage orders will flow over the next five years, relevant to diaspora investors in Indian power and battery supply chains.
